questions.question: In the FIRST DFS pass of Kosaraju's algorithm on graph G (alphabetical exploration), which vertex is the LAST to finish (placed at the TOP of the stack)?
questions.explanation: In Pass 1, DFS pushes vertices to the stack in order of finishing times. Vertex 'a' finishes last and sits at the top of the stack.

questions.question: In the SECOND DFS pass on the transposed graph G^T, which vertex serves as the starting root of the very FIRST component explored?
questions.explanation: Pass 2 processes vertices by popping from the Pass 1 stack. The first vertex popped from the stack top is 'a', becoming the first root in G^T.

questions.question: In the transposed graph G^T constructed during Kosaraju's algorithm, what is the out-degree (number of outgoing edges) of vertex 'e'?
questions.explanation: Transposing reverses every edge direction. The out-degree of 'e' in G^T equals its in-degree in the original graph G, which is 2.

questions.explanation: In any Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), no directed cycles can exist. Therefore, mutual reachability between distinct vertices is impossible, and every SCC is a singleton of size 1.
